deals.headline: Bill Foley's Black Knight takes 40% of FC Lorient through a EUR 10m capital increase
deals.investor: Black Knight Football and Entertainment (BKFE / BKFC, Bill Foley; backed by Cannae Holdings)
deals.summary: BKFE agreed a strategic partnership with FC Lorient: a capital increase giving it 40% for about EUR 10m (as reported by Ouest-France via Sportune), with Loïc Féry keeping control; Cannae described it as a 'significant minority interest' acquired in January 2023, and its 2026 10-Q confirms BKFC held 40% before January 2026.

deals.evidence: BKFC purchased the remaining 60% equity interest in FC Lorient
deals.headline: BKFC buys the remaining 60% of FC Lorient for USD 70.3m and becomes sole shareholder
deals.seller: Loïc Féry (former majority owner) and remaining holders
deals.summary: BKFC acquired the remaining 60% equity interest for total consideration of USD 70.3m, USD 40.7m in cash and USD 29.6m in BKFC stock; former majority owner Loïc Féry became a BKFC shareholder and stays president. The change of capital was presented to the DNCG before completion. Cannae's stake in BKFC fell to 42.7% as a result.

deals.date_text: Agreement in principle reported 31 October 2025; works expected from 2027

deals.headline: City of Lorient and FC Lorient agree in principle on financing a new west stand at the Moustoir (est. EUR 37m)
deals.investor: City of Lorient (with an FC Lorient contribution)
deals.summary: The municipal owner and the club reached an agreement in principle on financing the demolition and rebuild of the Moustoir's west stand, estimated at EUR 37m in total (other reports give EUR 33m of public money or about EUR 40m; the mayor says the club puts in EUR 3m). Delivery was envisaged for 2028; works have since slipped to spring 2027.

name: FC Lorient Bretagne Sud
notes: Season mismatch: the latest published accounts (DNCG 2024/25, K EUR, group perimeter incl. the association, distribution, training-centre and real-estate entities) cover a season FC Lorient played in Ligue 2; it returned to Ligue 1 for 2025-26. 'Revenue' is total non-transfer earnings; the EUR 1.1m pre-tax profit came from a EUR 40.5m profit on player trading against a EUR 38.9m operating loss. Financial debts EUR 9.3m and cash EUR 4.5m, but no net-debt figure is published. The January 2026 price is Cannae's SEC disclosure in USD (no EUR figure or valuation stated; Sportune's roughly EUR 60m is its own estimate of the final tranche and is not used). The 2023 EUR 10m / 40% terms come from press (Ouest-France via Sportune); Cannae's filings only say 'significant minority interest' for 2023 and '40%' before January 2026. The company register (recherche-entreprises) still lists Arnaud Tanguy as directeur général; the club says Benoit Muller took over on 20 April 2026, with Tanguy assisting until season end. Stadium renovation totals differ by source (EUR 33m public money, EUR 37m, about EUR 40m); the JAIME Radio figure is used. No shirt sponsor found on a club page; no honours, attendance, social or valuation figures recorded. Féry's 70% holding in Chenavari (London asset manager, about EUR 5bn under management) is from Challenges via Sportune (19 July 2026). Cannae's SEC filings (10-K, 10-Q) are the primary source for the 2026 price and for Cannae's 42.7% (January 2026) / 42.4% (30 June 2026) stake in BKFC; sec.gov only serves clients that declare a contact user agent.

ownership_summary: Since January 2026 FC Lorient has been wholly owned by Black Knight Football Club (BKFC), the multi-club partnership whose general partner is Bill Foley and which also owns AFC Bournemouth and a majority of Moreirense. BKFC entered in January 2023 with a capital increase giving it 40% for about EUR 10m, then bought the remaining 60% in January 2026 for USD 70.3m (USD 40.7m cash and USD 29.6m of BKFC stock, per Cannae's 10-K); long-time majority owner and president Loïc Féry rolled into BKFC as a shareholder and remains club president. NYSE-listed Cannae Holdings owns 42.7% of BKFC after the deal (42.4% at 30 June 2026).
